Subject: Orchestrated SDK adapter — initial scope and sprint proposal

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — excited about the possibility of tightly integrating LumenForge's prompt-management SDK into Redwood's orchestration/runtime so customers can get first-class tracing, prompt versioning, and metrics out-of-the-box.

Attached is a short scope sheet (redwood-lumenforge-scope-sheet.pdf) that outlines a 3-week technical sprint we think is realistic:
- Week 1: API mapping & auth (identify surface area + PKI/KMS flows)
- Week 2: Trace hook + sampling POC (LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter + telemetry shim)
- Week 3: Integration tests + rollout gating + docs

Open questions for you before we lock dates:
1) Which SDK surface(s) should we prioritize (prompt lifecycle, template store, or runtime instrumentation)?
2) Do you have a reference API spec for the SDK (auth + events) — if so please share.
3) Any legal/commercial constraints we should surface early (co-marketing, revenue share, or reseller terms)?

Proposed kickoff: May 17 (ET) — if that works on your side we can send calendar invites and spin up the shared Drive folder.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

Subject: Re: Orchestrated SDK adapter — initial scope and sprint proposal

Jonas — great write-up, thanks.

We think prioritizing runtime instrumentation + prompt lifecycle (template store) gives the clearest customer value. That lets us surface prompt diffs in traces and roll forward/back to previous prompt versions during retraining/debug.

I've attached our current API spec (lf-api-spec.md) which includes the events we emit (prompt.rendered, prompt.evaluation, prompt.rollback) and the auth header patterns. A few notes:
- We support OAuth2 service accounts and HMAC tokens — HMAC is easier for infra-only integrations.
- We emit sampling hints but leave sampling policy to the integrator (we can recommend defaults).

We can do May 17 kickoff; Alex and Priya will be on the call.

Alex
Alex Grant
VP Product, LumenForge

All — quick commercial / go-to-market questions from our side as we prep the SOW: 
- Will LumenForge require co-marketing credits or a revenue share for integrations? If so, what % or minimum commitments?
- Do you expect a single signed MOU or separate SOW + reseller addendum?
- Any IP constraints on joint assets (we typically co-own technical integration blogs but not product trademarks).

Also looping in a high-level ask: if LumenForge can commit a reference customer for an initial pilot, that materially shortens our enterprise sales cycle. Happy to discuss structure (short-term pilot credits, discounted bundle for the first 6 months).

Thanks — Marissa

Quick technical clarifications from infra:
- Telemetry: we need event contract stability for trace hooks (fields + types). Can you pin the event schema for the sprint? If the schema changes mid-sprint it will blow the test plan.
- Sampling: our default production sampling is 5% for prompt-level traces; for pilot customers we can raise to 25%. If LumenForge wants higher fidelity we should budget for additional egress/cost.
- Auth: prefer short-lived OAuth service account tokens (we can accept HMAC for initial POC).

I'll add a tech checklist to the Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwood-LumenForge-Integration) with SLI targets and test cases.

—Karthik
